classification.difficultyReason: Apply both graphical parity symmetries while preserving excluded endpoints, extrema, asymptotic behaviour and finite endpoints.

content.prompt: Complete the following diagrams to make the graphs represent: (i) even functions, (ii) odd functions.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 53, left column, first graph row
spec.description: Supplied positive left branch with a leftward continuation arrow and an open endpoint at (0,2). Separate canvas for the even completion.
spec.mathematics: Schematic contour only; no equation is asserted. The curve approaches the negative x-axis from above. The right half is blank.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied branch is visible. Its reflection is solution-only.

answer.short:
Symmetric positive branches, with $(0,2)$ left open.

Reflect in the $y$-axis.
answer.worked: For an even function, $f(-x)=f(x)$. Reflect the supplied branch in the $y$-axis. The new right branch approaches the positive $x$-axis from above. Keep the point $(0,2)$ open.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 53; answer PDF 29, printed page 607, Q53 left
spec.description: Complete even graph with two positive branches and one open point at (0,2).
spec.mathematics: The added branch is the exact y-axis reflection of the editable supplied contour. Both tails approach the x-axis from above.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete answer graph; answer editions only.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 53, left column, first graph row
spec.description: A second copy of the supplied branch for the incompatible odd completion.
spec.mathematics: Same contour, hole, coordinate frame and dimensions as the even-response canvas; no equation is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: The rotated right branch and its endpoint are absent from the question.

answer.short:
Add a negative right branch with an open point at $(0,-2)$; retain the open point at $(0,2)$.

Rotate the supplied branch $180^\circ$ about the origin.
answer.worked: For an odd function, $f(-x)=-f(x)$. Rotate the supplied branch $180^\circ$ about the origin, taking $(x,y)$ to $(-x,-y)$. The added branch lies below the positive $x$-axis and approaches it from below. Retain the open points at $(0,2)$ and $(0,-2)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 53; answer PDF 29, printed page 607, Q53 right
spec.description: Complete odd graph with branches in quadrants II and IV and open points at (0,2) and (0,-2).
spec.mathematics: The added contour is the exact half-turn of the supplied contour; both arrowed tails approach the x-axis.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete answer graph; answer editions only.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 54, left column, first graph row
spec.description: Left U-shaped branch, filled minimum (-1,1), dashed guides, open endpoint (0,2), and upper-left continuation arrow.
spec.mathematics: Only the labelled point coordinates are specified. The editable contour does not assert a quadratic equation.
spec.answerVisibility: The right side is an empty canvas for the even completion.

answer.short:
Add a minimum at $(1,1)$ and an upper-right tail; keep $(0,2)$ open.

Reflect in the $y$-axis.
answer.worked: Reflect every supplied point in the $y$-axis. The minimum $(-1,1)$ becomes $(1,1)$, with matching coordinate guides. The new branch rises to the right and approaches the same open point $(0,2)$ on the axis. This gives $f(-x)=f(x)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 54; answer PDF 29, printed page 607, Q54 left
spec.description: Even completion with filled minima at (-1,1) and (1,1), matching guides, two upward tails and an open point at (0,2).
spec.mathematics: The new branch, point and guides are obtained by exact x-coordinate reflection of the supplied geometry.
spec.answerVisibility: Complete answer graph; answer editions only.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 54, left column, first graph row
spec.description: Separate odd-response copy of the supplied branch, minimum, hole and guides.
spec.mathematics: Identical supplied geometry and coordinate frame to the even-response canvas.
spec.answerVisibility: No rotated branch, negative endpoint or right-hand extremum is supplied.

answer.short:
Add a maximum at $(1,-1)$, an open point at $(0,-2)$ and a downward-right tail.

Rotate the supplied branch $180^\circ$ about the origin.
answer.worked: Rotate the supplied graph $180^\circ$ about the origin. The filled minimum $(-1,1)$ becomes a filled maximum at $(1,-1)$, and the open endpoint $(0,2)$ becomes an open endpoint at $(0,-2)$. Rotate the coordinate guides and continuation arrow as well. Retain the original branch, giving $f(-x)=-f(x)$.

spec.mathematics: The added branch is obtained by negating both coordinates of the supplied branch.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 55, left column, second graph row
spec.description: A quadrant-III branch with leftward and downward arrows, approaching both axes without crossing them.
spec.mathematics: Unspecified reciprocal-like contour; no equation, numerical scale, point marker or additional tick is introduced.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied branch is visible; quadrant IV is available for the even completion.

answer.short:
Branches in quadrants III and IV, both below the $x$-axis.

Reflect in the $y$-axis.
answer.worked: Reflect the supplied branch in the $y$-axis. The new branch lies in quadrant IV, approaching the $y$-axis downward and the positive $x$-axis from below. Neither branch crosses an axis. The graph has $y$-axis symmetry, so the completed function is even.

Branches in quadrants III and I.

Rotate the supplied branch $180^\circ$ about the origin.
answer.worked: Rotate the supplied branch $180^\circ$ about the origin. The new branch lies in quadrant I, approaching the positive $y$-axis upward and the positive $x$-axis from above. Neither branch crosses an axis. The completed graph has the origin symmetry of an odd function.

spec.description: Finite negative arc from (-pi,0) to the origin, with a filled trough at (-pi/2,-1), dashed guides and source labels.
spec.mathematics: The arc is a schematic editable contour through the stated landmarks, not an asserted sine function. There are no curve continuation arrows or open endpoint rings.
spec.answerVisibility: No positive-x arc or transformed coordinate marker is visible.

answer.short:
Add a negative arc through $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},-1\right)$, ending at $(\pi,0)$.

Reflect in the $y$-axis.
answer.worked: Reflect the supplied arc in the $y$-axis. The trough $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},-1\right)$ becomes $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},-1\right)$, and $(-\pi,0)$ becomes $(\pi,0)$. The origin remains fixed. Add the matching guides and filled trough, retaining finite endpoints and no continuation arrows.

The origin remains fixed. Add the matching guides and filled crest, retaining finite endpoints and no continuation arrows.
